title: Database queries slow or timing out
symptoms: Queries take much longer than usual
root_cause: Blocking sessions, stale optimiser statistics or a missing index on a hot table.
diagnostic_steps: Check the database for long-running or blocked sessions during the slow period
Review the execution plan of the slowest query for full table scans
Check whether optimiser statistics on the affected tables are stale

steps: Ask the DBA to end the blocking session after confirming with its owner
Ask the DBA to gather fresh optimiser statistics on the affected tables
Re-run the report and confirm it completes within the normal time

escalation_criteria: a month-end or financial close process is blocked

title: Database connection pool exhausted
symptoms: Application cannot obtain a database connection
common_error_codes: Timeout expired. The timeout period elapsed prior to obtaining a connection from the pool
root_cause: Connections are leaked or the pool is sized below peak demand.
diagnostic_steps: Count active and idle sessions for the application account
Check the application log for connection leak warnings

steps: Ask the application team to recycle the application connection pool
Ask the DBA to review the session and process limits for the application account

title: Database login failed, access denied or account locked
symptoms: User cannot log in to the database
root_cause: The login does not exist, is not mapped to the database, uses the wrong credentials or is locked.
diagnostic_steps: Confirm the exact login name and the database the user is connecting to
Check the SQL Server error log for the 18456 state code or the Oracle audit trail
Check whether the account is locked or disabled

steps: Ask the DBA to create the login if it is missing and map it to the approved database role
Ask the DBA to unlock the account if it is locked
Have the user reconnect and confirm access

escalation_criteria: the account belongs to a service or batch job

title: Database password expired
symptoms: User is asked to change the password at login
root_cause: The database password policy expired the password.
diagnostic_steps: Confirm the error text mentions an expired password

steps: Have the user change the password through the approved self-service tool
Ask the DBA to reset the password if self-service is not available

escalation_criteria: the account belongs to a service or batch job

title: Database backup or restore failure
root_cause: The backup destination is full or unreachable.
diagnostic_steps: Check the backup job log for the failing step
Check free space on the backup destination

steps: Ask the DBA to free space or switch to the secondary backup destination
Ask the DBA to re-run the backup and confirm it completes

escalation_criteria: a restore is needed for production data

title: Laptop slow, hot or shutting down unexpectedly
root_cause: Blocked air vents, failing fan or sustained high CPU load.
diagnostic_steps: Check that the air vents are not blocked and the laptop is on a hard surface
Check Task Manager for processes using high CPU
Check the system event log for thermal or Kernel-Power 41 events

steps: Close or uninstall the process causing sustained high CPU
Book a hardware check for the fan and thermal paste

title: Laptop battery not charging
symptoms: Battery stays at the same percentage
root_cause: Faulty charger, worn battery or power-management driver issue.
diagnostic_steps: Try a known-good charger
Check the battery health report

steps: Update the battery and power-management drivers
Replace the battery if health is low

title: External monitor goes black, flickers or shows no signal
root_cause: Loose or faulty cable, or a display driver or refresh-rate mismatch after an update.
diagnostic_steps: Check the video cable is firmly connected at both ends and try a different cable
Note whether the problem started after a driver or operating system update
Test the monitor with a different laptop or port

steps: Roll back or update the display driver to the version approved by IT
Set the monitor refresh rate to 60 Hz in display settings
Restart the laptop and confirm the monitor stays on

title: Docking station not detected
symptoms: Peripherals on the dock do not work
root_cause: Dock firmware or driver out of date.
diagnostic_steps: Reconnect the dock and check the dock power light

steps: Update the dock firmware and driver

title: Printer not printing
symptoms: Print jobs stay in the queue
root_cause: Stuck print spooler or printer offline.
diagnostic_steps: Check the printer is online and has paper

steps: Clear the print queue and resend the job

title: USB device not recognised
root_cause: Faulty port, cable or USB driver.
diagnostic_steps: Try a different USB port
Check Device Manager for the device status

steps: Reinstall the USB device driver

title: Keyboard or mouse not responding
root_cause: Flat battery, lost wireless pairing or faulty receiver.
diagnostic_steps: Replace the batteries or charge the device
Try a different USB port for the receiver

steps: Re-pair the device with its receiver
Replace the device if it still does not respond

title: Bluetooth device will not pair
root_cause: Stale pairing record or Bluetooth driver issue.
diagnostic_steps: Check Bluetooth is enabled

steps: Remove the device and pair again

title: Internal application access request
symptoms: User needs access to an internal application
root_cause: The user is not in the approved access group for the application.
diagnostic_steps: Confirm the application name and the role the user needs

steps: Raise an access request for manager approval through the service catalogue

escalation_criteria: the request is for privileged access

title: Mailbox full or cannot send email
root_cause: The mailbox has reached its quota.
diagnostic_steps: Check the mailbox size against the quota

steps: Archive or delete old items to reduce the mailbox size

title: Shared drive cannot be mapped
root_cause: Path or permission problem.
diagnostic_steps: Check the share path

steps: Re-map the shared drive

title: Windows account locked out
root_cause: Repeated failed logins.
diagnostic_steps: Check for saved old passwords on other devices

steps: Unlock the account through the self-service portal

title: VPN will not connect or repeatedly disconnects
symptoms: VPN drops after a few minutes
root_cause: The assigned VPN gateway is unreachable or cached credentials or profiles are stale.
diagnostic_steps: Confirm the device has working internet access without the VPN
Check the VPN client log for 'Gateway not responding' and note the gateway name
Check whether colleagues on the same gateway are affected

steps: Restart the VPN client and reconnect
Connect to the alternate gateway listed in the VPN client profile
Clear the saved VPN credentials and sign in again

escalation_criteria: the gateway is down for all users

title: VPN slow or unstable while connected
symptoms: VPN is connected but very slow
VPN drops when the laptop is busy
root_cause: Local resource exhaustion or a congested gateway.
diagnostic_steps: Check endpoint CPU and memory usage while the VPN is connected
Run a speed test with and without the VPN

steps: Close high-CPU applications and reconnect the VPN

title: Cannot connect to corporate Wi-Fi
symptoms: Laptop does not see the corporate SSID
root_cause: Expired Wi-Fi certificate or disabled adapter.
diagnostic_steps: Check the wireless adapter is enabled
Check the Wi-Fi certificate has not expired

steps: Forget the network and reconnect with corporate credentials

escalation_criteria: no one in the building can connect

title: Wi-Fi connection drops intermittently
symptoms: Connection drops in one area of the building
root_cause: Access point overload, interference or roaming issues in one area.
diagnostic_steps: Check whether other devices in the same area also drop
Note the SSID, access point name and signal strength when the drop occurs

steps: Forget the network and reconnect
Update the wireless adapter driver to the version approved by IT

escalation_criteria: multiple managed devices disconnect in the same area

title: Web proxy blocks a site
root_cause: Proxy category policy.
diagnostic_steps: Confirm the URL and the block message

steps: Raise a proxy exception request

title: DNS name resolution failure
root_cause: Stale DNS cache or wrong DNS server assigned.
diagnostic_steps: Run nslookup for the failing name
Check which DNS servers the adapter is using

steps: Flush the DNS cache and reconnect to the network

title: Website certificate error
root_cause: Wrong system clock or expired certificate.
diagnostic_steps: Check the device date and time

steps: Correct the system time and reload the page

title: MFA prompt not received
root_cause: Authenticator app not registered on the new phone.
diagnostic_steps: Check the phone has network access

steps: Re-register the authenticator app

title: Software installation fails
root_cause: Another installation is running or prerequisites are missing.
diagnostic_steps: Check whether another installation is running

steps: Retry the installation from the software centre

title: Windows update fails
root_cause: Corrupt update cache.
diagnostic_steps: Check the update history for the failing update

steps: Retry the update from the software centre

title: Antivirus quarantined a file or reported a threat
root_cause: A file matched an antivirus signature.
diagnostic_steps: Record the threat name and file path from the antivirus console

steps: Leave the file in quarantine and report the alert to security operations

escalation_criteria: multiple devices report the same threat

title: Application crashes on start-up
root_cause: A faulty add-in, corrupt user profile or damaged installation.
diagnostic_steps: Open Event Viewer and find the 'Faulting application name' entry for the crash
Start the application in safe mode to check whether an add-in causes the crash

steps: Turn off the add-ins named in the crash log and restart the application
Run an Office repair from Apps & Features
Recreate the user profile for the application if the crash continues

escalation_criteria: the crash affects many users after a release

title: Application slow or high CPU/memory usage
root_cause: A runaway process or insufficient memory.
diagnostic_steps: Check Task Manager for the process using the most CPU and memory
Check whether the high usage starts with a specific application

steps: Close the runaway process and restart the application
Apply the latest approved update for the application
